docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text: The group travel industry faces significant operational challenges. Travel agencies, tour operators, and large organizations struggle to coordinate multiple groups simultaneously. Current workflows rely on a fragmented mix of WhatsApp for communication, Google Maps for location, and static PDF itineraries. This leads to communication breakdowns, safety risks (due to lack of real-time visibility), and operational inefficiency, preventing agencies from scaling their services effectively.Existing solutions often compromise on data privacy, real-time coordination, and auditability, making them unsuitable for professional or organized travel management.

docs.title: Proposed Solution
docs.text:
TrackUs is a centralized Group Travel Coordination Platform designed to streamline operations and enhance traveler safety.

  • For Organization: A single dashboard to manage hundreds of client groups, ensuring data privacy and operational control.
  • For Travelers: A seamless mobile experience for real-time itinerary updates, group chat, and safety tracking.
  • Business Value: reduces manual coordination time by 40%, improves incident response time with live tracking, and increases client retention through a premium branded experience.

TrackUs addresses these challenges with a multi-tenant, API-first backend.

  • It enforces strict data isolation using Tenant IDs across all entities (Users, Groups, Events).
  • It implements a 3-tier role system (Super Admin, Tenant Admin, User) to ensure granular access control for platform owners, agency managers, and travelers.
  • It provides real-time capabilities via WebSockets for live location tracking, instant group chat, and critical notifications.
  • It integrates background processing with Celery and Redis to handle asynchronous tasks like email notifications and data cleanup efficiently.

docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text: TrackUs is a multi-tenant travel coordination platform where data is strictly isolated by Tenant.

docs.title: Core Tenets
docs.text:
• A User belongs to exactly one Tenant.
  • A Group (travel party) belongs to exactly one Tenant.
  • Cross-tenant access is strictly blocked. Users cannot view or modify itineraries or location data from other tenants.

docs.title: User Roles
docs.text:
1. SUPER_ADMIN: Platform owner. Manages Tenants and Tenant Admins. Has system-wide oversight but does not participate in specific travel events.
  2. TENANT_ADMIN: Organization manager (e.g., Travel Agency Admin). Manages Users and Groups within their specific Tenant.
  3. USER: Standard traveler or member. Manages their own profile, joins groups, and participates in travel events.
  4. Group Admin: Admin of groups in an tenant.
  5. Group Member: Member of groups in an tenant.

docs.title: Key Capabilities
docs.text:
• Multi-Tenancy: Complete data isolation per organization/tenant.
  • Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Distinct permissions for platform admins, tenant managers, and end-users.
  • Real-Time Communication: WebSocket-based architecture for instant group chat and notifications.
  • Location Tracking: Secure real-time location sharing within travel groups to enhance member safety.
  • Event Management: Comprehensive scheduling for travel itineraries with participant management.
  • Scalable Architecture: Built on FastAPI and AsyncPG for high-performance asynchronous operations.

docs.title: 1. Multi-Tenancy Architecture
docs.text:
• Tenant-First Approach: Every user, group, and event is scoped to a specific Tenant ID.
  • Data Isolation:service-level checks ensure queries never leak data across tenant boundaries.
  • Tenant Management: Super Admins create and manage tenants, while Tenant Admins operate independently within them.

docs.title: 2. Advanced Permission System
docs.text:
• Super Admin: System maintenance, tenant creation, and platform-wide configuration.
  • Tenant Admin: Management of their tenant's users, creating travel groups, and overseeing events.
  • User: Varying levels of access to groups (Admin vs Member) and events (Accepted vs Invited).

docs.title: 3. Real-Time Systems
docs.text:
• WebSocket Manager: A robust connection manager handling user presence and message broadcasting.
  • Redis Pub/Sub: Scalable message distribution across server instances for chat and notifications.
  • Live Updates: Immediate feedback for location updates, new messages, and event status changes.

docs.title: 4. Travel & Event Management
docs.text:
• Group Coordination: Users are organized into Groups, allowing for persistent teams of travelers.
  • Itinerary Planning: Detailed event creation with start/end times, destinations, and auto-invitations for group members.
  • Participant State: Tracking of user responses (Accepted, Declined) and attendance status.
  • Soft Deletion: All major entities (Users, Groups, Events) support soft deletion to preserve history and prevent accidental data loss.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: Goal Description Multi-Tenancy Secure isolation of data across different travel agencies or organizations. RBAC Distinct roles (Super Admin, Tenant Admin, User) with specific privilege sets. Real-Time Low-latency communication and updates using WebSockets. Data Privacy Secure location sharing only within authorized groups. Scalability Async architecture designed to handle concurrent users and connections. Security JWT authentication, secure password hashing, and token usage validation.

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text: TrackUs follows a modern, asynchronous microservices-ready architecture built on FastAPI. It emphasizes real-time capabilities and strict tenant isolation.

docs.title: REST API
docs.text: Client → Load Balancer / Nginx → Uvicorn (ASGI Server) → FastAPI Router → Dependencies (Auth & Permissions) → Service Layer (Business Logic) → SQLAlchemy (Async ORM) → PostgreSQL Database

docs.title: Real-Time WebSockets
docs.text: Client → WebSocket Handshake → Connection Manager (app/realtime/manager.py) → Redis Pub/Sub (Message Broker) → Broadcaster (Fan-out to connected clients)

docs.title: Architectural Principles
docs.text:
• API-First Design: All functionalities are exposed via RESTful endpoints.
  • Real-Time First: Core features like Chat and Location are built on WebSockets for sub-200ms latency.
  • Separation of Concerns: Logic is decoupled into Routers, Services, and Schemas (Pydantic).
  • Multi-Tenancy: Data is logically isolated by tenant_id at the database level.
  • Soft Deletion: Entities (Groups, Events) are marked as deleted to preserve history.

docs.title: 1. Core Framework
docs.text:
• FastAPI: High-performance Python framework for building APIs.
  • SQLAlchemy (Async): Modern ORM for asynchronous database interactions.
  • Pydantic 2.0: Data validation and serialization.
  • PostgreSQL: Primary relational database with asyncpg driver.

docs.title: 2. Real-Time & Asynchronous
docs.text:
• WebSockets: Native FastAPI support for bidirectional communication.
  • Redis: In-memory data store acting as:
    • Pub/Sub Broker: Distributes chat messages and location updates across server instances.
    • Celery Broker: Queues background tasks.
    • Rate Limiting Backend: Prevents API abuse.
  • Celery: Distributed task queue for non-blocking operations.
    • Tasks: Sending emails (users.tasks), data cleanup (cleanup.tasks).
  • Celery Beat: Scheduler for periodic maintenance jobs.
    • Jobs: archive_old_events, prune_inactive_users.

docs.title: 3. Email Service
docs.text:
• SMTP Relay: Transactional emails sent via aiosmtplib.
    • Supports providers like Brevo (Sendinblue), SendGrid, or AWS SES via standard SMTP configuration.

docs.title: Modules Breakdown
docs.text: Module Description Key Components auth Identity & Access Management. JWT issuance, Refresh Tokens, Blacklisting. tenants Organization Management. Tenant model, onboarding flows. users User Profiles. User model, profile application. groups Team Management. Group (Team) management, membership logic. events Trip Management. TravelEvent (Trip) creation, itinerary planning. chat Communication. ChatMessage, EventMessage. WebSocket endpoints. location Live Tracking. Real-time coordinate processing, location history. notifications Alerts. In-app notifications via WebSocket.

docs.title: Service Layer Pattern
docs.text: Business logic is abstracted away from API routes into independent Service classes (e.g., GroupService, ChatService). This ensures: - Reusability: Logic can be called from API, Celery tasks, or WebSockets. - Testability: Services can be unit tested in isolation.

docs.title: Dependency Injection
docs.text: Authentication and permissions are injected into routes using FastAPI's Depends. - get_current_user: Validates JWT. - require_tenant_admin: Enforces RBAC. - get_db: Provides a scoped database session.

docs.title: Project Summary
docs.text: TrackUs successfully delivers a robust, scalable backend for modern Travel Agencies. By moving beyond simple CRUD operations to a real-time, event-driven architecture, the platform addresses the critical needs of safety, communication, and itinerary management in group travel.

docs.title: Key Achievements
docs.text:
1. Strict Multi-Tenancy:

    • Implemented a rigorous Organization (Tenant) isolation strategy.
    • Ensured data privacy where Agency A’s data is completely invisible to Agency B.
    • Secured via middleware and dependency injection patterns.

  2. Real-Time Safety Core:

    • Live Location: Built a low-latency WebSocket engine capable of tracking hundreds of participants simultaneously during Trips.
    • Instant Communication: Developed a persistent Team Chat and ephemeral Trip Chat using Redis Pub/Sub for cross-instance scaling.

  3. Complex Business Logic:

    • "Last Admin" Protection: Prevents groups from becoming orphaned by locking the removal of the final administrator.
    • Trip Lifecycle: Enforced a strict state machine (PLANNED -> ONGOING -> COMPLETED) to maintain data integrity.
    • User Lifecycle: Managed soft-deletion cascades that gracefully handle "ghost" users in active chats and trips.

  4. Modern Architecture:

    • Leveraged FastAPI for high performance.
    • Utilized Celery & Redis for reliable background processing (emails, cleanup).
    • Adhered to API-First principles with comprehensive documentation.

docs.title: Final Thoughts
docs.text: TrackUs is not just a database of trips; it is a safety and coordination engine. By prioritizing real-time connectivity and strict data boundaries, it creates a trusted environment for agencies to manage their most valuable asset—their travelers' experience.

docs.title: Database Schema
docs.text: TrackUs uses a relational database (PostgreSQL) with a multi-tenant schema design. All primary entities are linked to an Tenant.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text: This section outlines the functional and non-functional requirements of the TrackUs system.

docs.title: 1. Multi-Tenancy & Organizations
docs.text:
• The system must isolate data (Users, Teams, Trips, Chat) per Organization (Tenant).
  • New registrations must automatically provision an Organization.
  • An Organization represents a company or agency (e.g., "Acme Travel").
  • If an Organization is deactivated, access triggers appropriate blocks for all its members.

docs.title: 2. User Management
docs.text:
• Roles: Must support Super Admin, Tenant Admin (Org Admin), and User (Traveler/Employee).
  • Authentication: JWT-based login, refresh, and logout (blacklist).
  • Email Verification: Users should verify email before becoming fully active.
  • Tenant Admin Control: Tenant Admins can manage users within their organization only.

docs.title: 3. Team & Trip Management
docs.text:
• Hierarchical Structure:
    • Groups (Teams/Projects): Represents a persistent team or project within the Organization (e.g., "Python Team", "Summer Campaign Project").
    • Events (Trips/Outings): Specific activities or trips organized for a Team (e.g., "Sunday Outing", "Manali Trip").
  • Ownership: Teams created by Tenant Admins or Users.
  • Visibility:
    • Tenant Admin: View all Teams/Trips in the Org.
    • User: View only Teams they are part of.
  • Soft Deletion: Teams and Trips are marked deleted, maintaining history.

docs.title: 4. Real-Time Communication
docs.text:
• Group Chat: Persistent chat history for all Group members.
  • Event Chat: Temporary/Focused chat for specific Event participants.
  • Live Location:
    • Real-time coordinate sharing for active Event participants.
    • Automatic last location tracking .

docs.title: 5. Notifications & Alerts
docs.text:
• Email: For account verification, password resets..
  • In-App/Push: For add in group , remove from group, event invite, and event cancel.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Strict Object-Level Permissions: Enforced via app/dependencies/
  • No Cross-Tenant Data Leakage: Middleware ensures Tenant ID isolation.
  • Secure WebSocket: Connections authenticated via JWT.

docs.title: Reliability
docs.text:
• Connection Recovery: WebSockets must handle disconnection/reconnection gracefully.
  • Data Integrity: Soft deletion ensures referential integrity for historical analysis.
  • Asynchronous Processing: Heavy tasks (emails, data cleanup) offloaded to Celery.

docs.title: Workflows & Edge Cases
docs.text: This document outlines the core business logic flows and specific edge cases handled by TrackUs.

docs.title: Hierarchy & Onboarding
docs.text:
1. Organization Setup: Super Admin creates a Tenant (Organization) and a Tenant Admin.
  2. User Onboarding: Tenant Admin creates Users (Travelers/Guides).
    • Constraint: Users are strictly bound to a single Tenant.

docs.title: Account Lifecycle
docs.text:
• Verification: New users are created as is_active=False. They must verify via email token to login.
  • Soft Deletion: Deleting a user does not remove them from the DB.
    • Cascade Effects:
      • Removed from all Teams (Groups).
      • Status set to LEFT in all future/active Trips (Events).
      • Live Location tracking disabled.
      • Auth tokens invalidated (forced logout).
  • Hard Deletion: A nightly Celery task (cleanup.tasks) permanently wipes users soft-deleted > 30 days ago.

docs.title: Creation & Ownership
docs.text:
• Any user can create a Group. The creator automatically becomes the First Admin.
  • Edge Case: The Last Admin
    • Rule: A Group MUST always have at least one Admin.
    • Constraint: The last remaining Admin cannot leave the group or demote themselves. They must promote another member first or delete the group entirely.

docs.title: Membership & Chat
docs.text:
• Adding Members: Only Admins can add members.
    • Effect: Added user gets access to Group Chat history immediately.
  • Removing Members:
    • Database: left_at timestamp is set.
    • Real-Time: If the user is online in the Chat, their WebSocket connection is forcefully severed (1008 Policy Violation).

docs.title: 3. Trip (Event) Lifecycle
docs.text: Trips follow a strict state machine to ensure data consistency.

docs.title: State Transitions
docs.text:
From To Trigger Notes PLANNED ONGOING Admin Action Trip start. Live Location becomes active. PLANNED CANCELLED Admin Action Trip cancelled. Participants notified. ONGOING COMPLETED Admin Action Trip end. Location tracking stops. ONGOING CANCELLED Admin Action Emergency stop.
  • Edge Case: You cannot revert a COMPLETED or CANCELLED event to PLANNED.
  • Edge Case: Live Location updates are rejected if the event is not ONGOING.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. Auto-Invite: When a Trip is created, all Team members are automatically INVITED.
    • Creator: Automatically ACCEPTED.
  2. Response: Members must explicitly ACCEPT or REJECT.
  3. Participation: Only ACCEPTED participants can share location and view the Event Chat.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text: • Creator Lock: The Trip creator cannot leave the Trip. They must cancel the event or delete it.

docs.title: WebSocket Disconnection
docs.text:
• Network Implementation: Uses Redis Pub/Sub to sync state across server instances.
  • Flow:
    1. User connects -> Authenticated via JWT.
    2. User removed from Team/Trip (via API).
    3. Server publishes "Disconnect" signal to Redis.
    4. All server instances check their active sockets and close the connection for that User ID.

docs.title: Live Location Edge Cases
docs.text:
• Ghosting: If a user loses internet, their location remains "stale". The frontend shows the "Last Updated" timestamp.
  • Permission Revocation: If a user's role changes from ACCEPTED to LEFT mid-trip, their location stream is immediately cut off.

docs.title: 6. Organization Deactivation
docs.text: If a Super Admin deactivates an Organization (is_active=False): 1. Login Block: No user from that Tenant can log in. 2. API Block: All active sessions are effectively killed (token validation checks user.is_active and tenant.is_active). 3. Background Tasks: Scheduled emails or notifications for that Tenant are skipped.
